title: Seeing fit: ease, drag lines and an accurate fitting

say: Seeing fit: ease, drag lines and an accurate fitting.
This is the video for module 1 of Fashion Basics and Clothing Alterations.
Most clients walk in with a feeling: it is not sitting well. Your first job is to turn that into a clear problem you can measure.

say: Ease is the difference between the body and the garment at the same place. If her bust is 96 cm and the blouse measures 104 cm, the blouse has 8 cm of ease.

panel.heading: The room between body and cloth
items: Ease = garment measurement minus body
Wearing ease: room to breathe, sit, move
Design ease: extra room for a style
Ask how she will wear the garment

say: Wearing ease is the minimum room to breathe, sit and move. A common guide for a fitted woven garment is about 2.5 cm at the waist.

panel.heading: The room between body and cloth
items: Ease = garment measurement minus body

say: Design ease is extra room added on purpose, like in a kaftan. Take it all out and it pulls at the hips when she sits.

say: A drag line is a fold or wrinkle, and its direction points to the cause. Horizontal pulling lines across the hips of a skirt mean the hip is too tight.

panel.heading: The garment shows you the problem

cards.d: Fine wrinkles stretched across the body, like rays. The area is too tight.
Soft, deep folds that hang. There is too much room there.
Lines at an angle point to the part that needs more or less length or width.

say: Vertical folds at the back waist of a dress mean too much width there.

say: Diagonal lines point to the part that needs more or less length or width. Look first, then measure, then decide. Never pin before you understand the cause.

say: For example, Halima, a bank officer in Kaduna, says her fitted dress hangs like a sack at the waist. Lay the dress flat, close it, measure across and double the number.
The bust has 6 cm of ease. That is normal wearing ease, so leave it.

panel.heading: Too big, or just loose?
items: Bust: 102 minus 96 = 6 cm. Leave it.
Waist: 98 minus 80 = 18 cm. Far too much.
Hip: 110 minus 104 = 6 cm. Comfortable.
Target waist 84 cm: remove 14 cm

say: The waist has 18 cm of ease, far more than the 2.5 cm guide.

say: She sits all day, so you agree about 4 cm of waist ease. 80 plus 4 is 84. So 14 cm comes out at the waist, tapering to nothing at bust and hip.

say: The fitting is the most important 15 minutes of the job. Ask her to bring the shoes and underwear she will wear.

panel.heading: Look, test, then pin top down
items: Right side out, closed, in her event shoes
Walk around her and look first
Ask her to sit, raise arms and bend
Pin shoulders, bust, waist, hip, hem last
Pin evenly on both sides
She checks the mirror and agrees

say: Look before you pin. Then ask her to sit and raise her arms. Some garments look perfect standing and pull badly sitting.

say: Pin from the top down, with the hem last, because changes higher up can change the length lower down. Pinch the same amount on left and right.

say: Let her look in the mirror and agree. Then read your fitting card back to her, and send her a photo of it.

say: Floors and bodies are not perfectly level, so do not fold up the same amount all round.

panel.heading: Measure from the floor
left: Fold up the same amount all round

say: Measure a fixed height from the floor, with a pin every 8 to 10 cm. You move, she stands still.
For example, Tunde's trousers drag. With his shoes on, the new inside leg is 76 cm instead of 82, so you shorten by 6 cm.

panel.heading: Measure from the floor
left: Fold up the same amount all round

say: Give her a private space to change. Tell her before you touch her, and keep your hands on the garment. A child's parent or guardian stays in the room.
Count your pins out and back in, and sweep the floor with a magnet after every session.

panel.heading: Every fitting
items: A private, curtained space to change
Tell her before you touch: hands on cloth
A child? A parent or guardian stays
Count pins out and back in
Sweep the floor with a magnet

say: Every alteration moves lines. A hem ending at the narrowest part of the leg usually looks lighter. Describe what the garment does, never criticise her body.

panel.heading: Show options, then let her choose
items: Vertical lines lengthen the look
Hems and waists are lines the eye stops on
Pin two options so she can see
Say no when the result will disappoint

say: For example, Grace wants her pencil skirt at the knee, which would remove the slit. You pin knee and midi lengths. She sees both and chooses midi, with confidence.

panel.heading: Show options, then let her choose
items: Vertical lines lengthen the look

say: If a seam holds only 1 cm, or satin will show old needle holes, say so before you start. An honest no keeps your reputation.

say: To remember. Ease is garment minus body. Pulling means tight, bagging means loose. Fit in her event shoes and pin top down. Mark hems from the floor. Write numbers she confirms.

panel.heading: Remember
items: Ease = garment minus body at the same place
Pulling means tight, bagging means loose
Fit in her shoes; pin top down, hem last
Mark hems at a fixed height from the floor
Record numbers and places she confirms

say: Check the ease on two of your own garments, run a mock fitting with a friend and fill in a fitting card, and pin two styling options to compare.
